ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram shows a 3 V supply connected through a 1 kΩ collector resistor to the collector of an NPN transistor. The transistor emitter is connected to ground. The base is driven from the left through a resistor, with the input base current labeled I_B. Reasoning: In saturation, use V_CE(sat) = 0.2 V. The voltage across the 1 kΩ collector resistor is therefore 3 V - 0.2 V = 2.8 V. The collector current is I_C = 2.8 V / 1 kΩ = 2.8 mA. With β = 50, the minimum base current needed to support this collector current is I_B = I_C / β = 2.8 mA / 50 = 0.056 mA = 56 μA.
